title: Gluing module sheaf objects over a covering of a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $U$ be an object and $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ a covering family, with $I$ a set in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C/U$, and use the restrictions $A_i,A_{ij},A_{ijk}$ to the slice sites over $U_i$, $U_i\times_U U_j$, and $U_i\times_U U_j\times_U U_k$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $F_i$ be $A_i$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and let $\phi_{ij}:F_i|_{U_i\times_U U_j}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_j|_{U_i\times_U U_j}$ be $A_{ij}$-linear isomorphisms for every pair, including equal indices. Assume $\phi_{ik}=\phi_{jk}\circ\phi_{ij}$ after restriction to every triple fibre product. Then there exists an $A$-module sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal C/U$ and $A_i$-linear isomorphisms $e_i:F|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_i$ such that $\phi_{ij}\circ e_i|_{U_i\times_U U_j}=e_j|_{U_i\times_U U_j}$ for all $i,j$.

source.place: Tag 04TR, sites-lemma-glue-sheaves, with the abelian-group and module operations on the compatible tuples; applies to any ring sheaf and covering, not only open or monomorphic covers.

proof.text: For an object $V\to U$, put $V_i=U_i\times_U V$ and $V_{ij}=U_i\times_U U_j\times_U V$. Define $F(V)$ to be the set of tuples $(s_i)\in\prod_i F_i(V_i)$ satisfying $\phi_{ij}(s_i|_{V_{ij}})=s_j|_{V_{ij}}$ for every pair. For a morphism $W\to V$ over $U$, restrict each component along $U_i\times_U W\to V_i$. Naturality of $\phi_{ij}$ preserves the compatibility equations; identity and composite restriction laws hold componentwise. All these fibre products exist by the base-change axiom for coverings.

source.place: Tag 04TR, sites-lemma-glue-sheaves: compatible-tuples formula; explicit verification of restrictions, sheaf condition and local isomorphisms omitted in the source.

proof.text: Make $F(V)$ an $A(V)$-module by $(s+t)_i=s_i+t_i$, $0_i=0$, $(-s)_i=-s_i$, and $(a s)_i=(a|_{V_i})s_i$. On $V_{ij}$ both scalar restrictions are $a|_{V_{ij}}$; linearity of $\phi_{ij}$ therefore preserves the tuple equations for all four operations. Every module axiom holds in each $F_i(V_i)$ and hence in the tuple subset. The restriction maps are additive and satisfy $(a s)|_W=a|_W(s|_W)$ by the corresponding property in each $F_i$.

source.place: Tag 04TR, sites-lemma-glue-sheaves: compatible-tuples formula; explicit verification of restrictions, sheaf condition and local isomorphisms omitted in the source.

proof.text: Let $\{W_b\to V\}_b$ be a covering in $\mathcal C/U$, and let $t^{(b)}\in F(W_b)$ be a matching family. For each $i$, the base-changed family $\{U_i\times_U W_b\to V_i\}_b$ is a covering of $\mathcal C/U_i$; its matching sections $t_i^{(b)}$ have a unique amalgamation $s_i\in F_i(V_i)$. On $V_{ij}$, the sections $\phi_{ij}(s_i|_{V_{ij}})$ and $s_j|_{V_{ij}}$ agree on the covering $\{V_{ij}\times_V W_b\to V_{ij}\}_b$, since each $t^{(b)}$ is a compatible tuple. Separatedness of $F_j$ makes them equal. Thus $(s_i)\in F(V)$ amalgamates the family, uniquely by separatedness in every component. The underlying presheaf is a sheaf, so the module presheaf of step 2 is an $A$-module sheaf.

proof.text: Fix $k$ and $g:W\to U_k$. For $s\in F(W)$ define $e_k(W)(s)$ by restricting $s_k\in F_k(U_k\times_U W)$ along the graph $d_g=(g,\mathrm{id}_W):W\to U_k\times_U W$. For $t\in F_k(W)$ define a tuple $q_k(W)(t)$ whose $i$-component is $\phi_{ki}(t|_{U_i\times_U W})$, evaluated on $U_i\times_U W$ as an object over $U_k\times_U U_i$ via $(g\circ\mathrm{pr}_W,\mathrm{pr}_{U_i})$. Restricting the cocycle $\phi_{kj}=\phi_{ij}\circ\phi_{ki}$ to $U_i\times_U U_j\times_U W$ gives its tuple equation. Thus $q_k$ takes values in $F(W)$. Both $e_k$ and $q_k$ commute with restriction by naturality of $\phi$ and the graph maps, and are $A(W)$-linear by step 2 and linearity of the transition maps.

source.place: Tag 04TR, sites-lemma-glue-sheaves: compatible-tuples formula; explicit verification of restrictions, sheaf condition and local isomorphisms omitted in the source.

proof.text: Restrict the $(k,k,k)$ cocycle to the full diagonal $U_k\to U_k\times_U U_k\times_U U_k$. The resulting automorphism $\alpha=\Delta^*\phi_{kk}$ satisfies $\alpha=\alpha\circ\alpha$, so cancellation gives $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. It follows that $e_k(W)q_k(W)(t)=t$. Conversely, restrict the tuple equation $\phi_{ki}(s_k)=s_i$ to $U_i\times_U W$ by the map with coordinates $(g\circ\mathrm{pr}_W,\mathrm{pr}_{U_i},\mathrm{pr}_W)$. Its left side is exactly the $i$-component of $q_k(W)e_k(W)(s)$, while its right side is $s_i$. Hence $q_ke_k=\mathrm{id}$ componentwise. Therefore $e_k:F|_{U_k}\to F_k$ is an $A_k$-linear isomorphism; no covering arrow was assumed monomorphic.

source.place: Tag 04TR, sites-lemma-glue-sheaves: compatible-tuples formula; explicit verification of restrictions, sheaf condition and local isomorphisms omitted in the source.

proof.text: For an object $W\to U_i\times_U U_j$ write $g_i,g_j$ for its two projections to $U_i,U_j$. Pull the tuple equation on $U_i\times_U U_j\times_U W$ back along $(g_i,g_j,\mathrm{id}_W)$. It gives $\phi_{ij}(e_i(W)(s))=e_j(W)(s)$ for every $s\in F(W)$. These are equalities of $A(W)$-linear maps, and hence the required equalities of $A_{ij}$-module sheaf morphisms on the overlap. The sheaf $F$ and the isomorphisms $e_i$ now meet every clause of the statement.
